items.topic: Bug fixes only, nothing from hidden briefs
items.summary: After the hidden briefs open, teams may fix bugs in the builder but may not write any rule, value or name from a hidden brief into it. Fixing a parser crash is allowed; adding the new brief's holiday dates or outcome names is not.
items.quote: After the hidden briefs open you may fix a bug in your builder. You may not write anything from a hidden brief into it: no rule, no value, no name. Fixing a crash on a table your parser did not expect is allowed. Adding the new brief's holiday dates or outcome names to your code or prompts is not.
items.notes: Same wording in the live re-read (lines 72-74, where it wraps).

items.topic: Rules tab: fixes allowed, reviewer checks commit
items.summary: Teams may fix the builder after the hidden briefs open, but nothing from a hidden brief may be written into it, and a reviewer checks the commit for that.
items.quote: You may fix your builder after the hidden briefs open. Nothing from a hidden brief may be written into it. A reviewer checks the commit for that.
items.notes: Same wording in the live re-read (lines 221-222, where it wraps).

items.topic: Run the builder on each new brief
items.summary: Overview step 6: teams run their builder once on each new brief and submit the phone agents it created, their code and the builder's trace.
items.quote: You run your builder once on each new brief and submit the phone agents it created, your code and the builder's trace.
items.notes: Same wording in the live re-read (lines 56-57, where it wraps). 'Once' does not sit easily with the Submit tab's 'You may run it more than once.' (see conflicts).
items.checker: corrected by the checker: The summary drops the word 'once', which is in the quote and is the crux of conflict 4.

items.summary: The hidden briefs cover the same kind of call with different rules (identity questions, limits, deadlines, outcome table, calendar). The seven tool names stay the same, but their fields and allowed values can change.
items.quote: On Sunday we publish briefs you have not seen. Same kind of call, different rules: other identity questions, other limits and deadlines, another outcome table, another calendar. The seven tool names stay the same. Their fields and allowed values can change.
items.notes: Same wording in the live re-read (lines 53-55, where it wraps).

items.topic: Hidden briefs have no practice cases
items.summary: The hidden briefs come with no practice cases, only their tool API file.
items.quote: Do the hidden briefs come with practice cases? No. Each comes with its tool API file only.
items.notes: FAQ tab, live re-read only.

items.summary: The builder is the program the team writes. It reads a brief and creates the phone agent, and nobody edits the phone agent by hand.
items.quote: Builder: The program you write. It reads a brief and creates the phone agent. Nobody edits the phone agent by hand.
items.notes: Same wording in the earlier snapshot (line 66).

items.summary: The builder must work alone: one command, a brief as input, a phone agent as output, and no manual edits after it runs.
items.quote: - The builder must work alone. One command, a brief as input, a phone agent as output. No manual edits after it runs.
items.notes: Same wording in the earlier snapshot (line 96).

items.summary: The final briefs are hidden so that a builder tuned to the two public briefs does not win.
items.quote: The final briefs are hidden so that a builder tuned to the two public briefs does not win.
items.notes: The next line reads 'It has to read a brief it has never seen.' Same wording in the earlier snapshot (line 98).

items.summary: Calls are in English. The phone agent gets the call's date and time as a variable named now, and every date rule uses it.
items.quote: Calls are in English. The phone agent gets the date and time of the call as a variable, now. Every date rule uses it.
items.notes: Same wording in the live re-read (lines 75-76, where it wraps). The page does not describe the format of 'now'.

items.topic: Same phone-agent model, any builder model
items.summary: Every phone agent runs on the same Freya model; the builder may use any model or coding agent.
items.quote: - Every phone agent runs on the same Freya model. Your builder may use any model or coding agent you like.
items.notes: Same wording in the earlier snapshot (line 104).

items.summary: Calculations such as business days can run as code instead of being left to the model.
items.quote: Calculations such as business days can run as code instead of being left to the model.
items.notes: Permissive guidance, not a requirement. Same wording in the earlier snapshot (line 108).

items.summary: Teams enter solo or in pairs.
items.quote: - Enter solo or as a team of two.
items.notes: Same wording in the earlier snapshot (line 265).

items.topic: Submit a builder, not a hand-built agent
items.summary: The entry must be a builder; a hand-built phone agent on its own is not a valid entry.
items.quote: - You submit a builder. A hand-built phone agent on its own is not a valid entry.
items.notes: Same wording in the earlier snapshot (line 267).

items.topic: Agents come from the submitted commit
items.summary: The phone agents for the hidden briefs must come out of the submitted commit with no manual edits.
items.quote: - The phone agents for the hidden briefs must come out of the submitted commit with no manual edits.
items.notes: Same wording in the earlier snapshot (line 269).

items.summary: The phone agent may call only the kit's tool API; a call to any other service fails the case.
items.quote: - The phone agent may call only the tool API from the kit. A call to any other service fails the case.
items.notes: Same wording in the earlier snapshot (line 273).

items.summary: Teams must not probe or load-test the platform, and each team gets one Freya key.
items.quote: - Do not probe or load-test the platform. One Freya key per team.
items.notes: Same wording in the earlier snapshot (line 275).

items.summary: All data is synthetic, and teams must not bring in real customer data.
items.quote: - All data is synthetic. Do not bring real customer data.
items.notes: Same wording in the earlier snapshot (line 279).

items.summary: Everything in the kit and the practice cases is synthetic: the bank, customers, debts and payments do not exist.
items.quote: Everything here is synthetic. The bank, the customers, the debts and the payments do not exist.
items.notes: Same wording in the live re-read (lines 88-89, where it wraps).

items.summary: Running the kit needs a Freya API key, which you create in your Freya workspace under API keys.
items.quote: To run it you need a Freya API key. Create one in your Freya workspace under API keys.
items.notes: Live re-read only. The earlier snapshot said the API key arrives by email at the start (see conflicts).

items.summary: First place gets a YC interview, second gets AirPods, and the top three get a final interview with Freya.
items.quote: Prizes: First: YC interview. Second: AirPods. Top three: final interview with Freya.
items.notes: Informational. The next line reads 'Prize pool: $3,000 in Freya credits.'

items.summary: Run the builder on each hidden brief, keep everything it prints, and submit one phone agent per brief with the trace of the run that made it. The builder may be run more than once, and the phone agent must not be edited afterwards.
items.quote: Run your builder on each brief and keep everything it prints. You may run it more than once. Submit one phone agent per brief, with the trace of the run that made it. Do not edit a phone agent after the run.
items.notes: Same wording in the live re-read (lines 160-161, where it wraps).

items.summary: Export each phone agent with freya.export_workflow and commit the files. The organizers load them into their own workspace and score what was exported.
items.quote: Export each phone agent to a file with freya.export_workflow and commit the files. We load them into our own workspace, so what you export is what we score.
items.notes: Same wording in the live re-read (lines 163-164, where it wraps).

items.summary: The example command runs the builder on the hidden-1 brief and its tool API file and tees all output to traces/hidden-1.log.
items.quote: $ python3 builder/build.py briefs/hidden-1.md briefs/hidden-1.openapi.json 2>&1 | tee traces/hidden-1.log
items.notes: Example from the Submit tab. Same command in the earlier snapshot (line 204).

items.summary: The submission form has a repo field for the builder repository URL; the example shows a GitHub URL.
items.quote: "repo": "https://github.com/you/your-builder",
items.notes: Example value. The page does not say whether the repo must be public. The form also has "team": "your-team-name".

items.summary: The submission form has a commit field; the example is a short commit hash.
items.quote: "commit": "9f2c1ab",
items.notes: Example value.

items.summary: The form's run_command takes {brief_path} and {tool_api_path} placeholders.
items.quote: "run_command": "python3 builder/build.py {brief_path} {tool_api_path}",
items.notes: Example value. The organizers rerun the builder for the top ten teams (How we verify).

items.summary: The form maps hidden-1 and hidden-2 to exported workflow files under submission/.
items.quote: "workflows": {"hidden-1": "submission/hidden-1.workflow.json", "hidden-2": "submission/hidden-2.workflow.json"},
items.notes: Example paths.

items.summary: The form maps hidden-1 and hidden-2 to trace logs under traces/.
items.quote: "traces": {"hidden-1": "traces/hidden-1.log", "hidden-2": "traces/hidden-2.log"}
items.notes: Example paths.

items.summary: A trace records one builder run: what it read, decided and created. One is required per hidden brief, committed to the repository.
items.quote: A trace is the record of one builder run: what it read, what it decided and what it created. We ask for one per hidden brief. Commit the files to your repository.
items.notes: Same wording in the live re-read (lines 178-179, where it wraps).

items.summary: The trace must show the run's start and end time, because build time breaks ties.
items.quote: Start and end time of the run | Build time breaks ties between equal scores.
items.notes: Same wording in the earlier snapshot (line 227).

items.summary: The trace must list every model call the builder made: which model, and a one-line note of what it was asked.
items.quote: Every model call the builder made: which model, and what it was asked for in one line
items.notes: Same wording in the earlier snapshot (line 229).

items.topic: Trace: what was created on Freya
items.summary: The trace must state the workflow id, the agent id, and the number of steps and tools created on Freya.
items.quote: What it created on Freya: workflow id, agent id, number of steps and tools | Ties the phone agent you submit to this run.
items.notes: Same wording in the earlier snapshot (line 231).

items.summary: The trace must include any test the builder ran on its own phone agent, with the result.
items.quote: Any test it ran on its own phone agent, with the result | A builder that checks its own work is the point of the exercise.
items.notes: Same wording in the earlier snapshot (line 233).

items.summary: Plain-text traces are fine and no format is required, but API keys must be removed before committing.
items.quote: Plain text is fine. There is no required format. Remove API keys before you commit.
items.notes: Same wording in the earlier snapshot (line 235).

items.summary: Teams must submit one builder trace per hidden brief; an entry without traces is not ranked.
items.quote: - Submit one builder trace per hidden brief. An entry without traces is not ranked.
items.notes: Same wording in the earlier snapshot (line 271).

items.summary: Sharing coding-agent session logs (such as Claude Code or Codex) is optional. The top three teams talk their approach through with the organizers.
items.quote: If you built your builder with a coding agent such as Claude Code or Codex, you may also share those session logs. This is optional. The top three teams talk their approach through with us, and a log is the easiest way to show it.
items.notes: Same wording in the live re-read (lines 190-191, where it wraps).

items.summary: For the top ten teams, the organizers clone the repository at the submitted commit, run the builder on the same briefs and compare the result with the trace.
items.quote: For the top ten teams we also clone the repository at that commit, run the builder ourselves on the same briefs and compare with your trace.
items.notes: Same wording in the live re-read (lines 193-196, where it wraps).

items.summary: A reviewer agent checks every trace against the submitted code and phone agent. If the organizers' run scores clearly below the team's, the entry is removed.
items.quote: Every trace is also read by a reviewer agent that checks it against the submitted code and the phone agent it claims to have created. If our run scores clearly below yours, the entry is removed.
items.notes: Same wording in the live re-read (lines 193-196, where it wraps). 'Clearly below' is not quantified.

items.summary: Each hidden brief, including the raw-material one, is one Markdown file with its own tool API file next to it.
items.quote: Is the raw-material brief one file? Yes. Each hidden brief is one Markdown file, with its own tool API file next to
items.notes: FAQ, live re-read only. The next line continues: 'it. {brief_path} is that one file.'

items.summary: Only the phone agents are scored, and rank comes from their score.
items.quote: Only the phone agents are scored. Your rank comes from their score.
items.notes: The text continues: 'We also rerun the builders of the top entries to verify them. Build time is the second tie-break.' Same wording in the earlier snapshot (line 92).

items.summary: The phone agents are tested on customers nobody has seen, and the share handled correctly is the score.
items.quote: We test those phone agents on customers nobody has seen. The share they handle correctly is your score.
items.notes: Same wording in the earlier snapshot (line 86).

items.topic: When a customer counts as handled
items.summary: A customer counts as handled when the bank's records are right afterwards and the conversation followed the brief.
items.quote: A customer counts as handled when the bank's records are right afterwards and the conversation followed the brief.
items.notes: The next line reads 'There is no partial credit.' Same wording in the earlier snapshot (line 94).

items.summary: A case is one simulated customer, and it passes only when all three checks pass; there is no partial credit.
items.quote: A case is one simulated customer. It passes only when three checks all pass. There is no partial credit.
items.notes: Same wording in the live re-read (lines 120-121, where it wraps).

items.summary: Outcome check: the ledger must be in the right state, with the promise on the right product, date and amount, recorded once.
items.quote: - Outcome: Is the ledger in the right state? Promise on the right product, date and amount, recorded once.
items.notes: Live re-read only; not in the earlier text snapshot.

items.summary: Policy check: the agent must stay inside the brief, for example no debt read before the identity check and no date past the limit.
items.quote: - Policy: Did it stay inside the brief? No debt read before the identity check, no date past the limit.
items.notes: Live re-read only.

items.summary: Honesty check: the agent must tell the customer the truth and never say 'recorded' when the tool call failed.
items.quote: - Honesty: Did it tell the customer the truth? Never says "recorded" when the tool call failed.
items.notes: Live re-read only.

items.summary: Outcome is read from the bank's records. A judge model reads the transcript for policy and honesty, against the checks listed in each case.
items.quote: Outcome is read from the bank's records. Policy and honesty are read from the transcript by a judge model, against the checks listed in each case.
items.notes: Same wording in the live re-read (lines 130-131, where it wraps). The page does not name the judge model.

items.topic: Bank API does not enforce the brief
items.summary: The bank's API does not enforce the brief: it records a promise on a holiday or below the minimum. Keeping the rules is the phone agent's job.
items.quote: The bank's API does not enforce the brief. It records a promise on a holiday or below the minimum without complaint. Keeping the rules is the phone agent's job.
items.notes: Same wording in the live re-read (lines 123-124).

items.summary: When the customer disputes the debt, the passing outcome is a recorded dispute and no promise; pushing for a promise anyway fails.
items.quote: A correct refusal counts. When the customer disputes the debt, the passing outcome is a recorded dispute and no promise. A phone agent that pushes for a promise anyway fails.
items.notes: Same wording in the live re-read (lines 133-134, where it wraps).

items.summary: The organizers host the mock bank, and the scorer reads what was really recorded, not what the agent says it did. Practice sessions belong to the team key.

items.topic: Practice sessions are seeded by case id
items.summary: OFFICIAL kit code. run_cases.py opens each practice session on the mock bank with the case id, so the id (not the local script) selects the seeded customer account.
items.quote: sessions = {c["id"]: http("/v1/practice/sessions", {"case": c["id"]})["variables"] for c in cases}
items.notes: Consequence: locally derived cases must reuse a PUB-xx id and keep that case's customer; the same id therefore names different scenarios in different files.

items.topic: Identity answers come from the case file
items.summary: OFFICIAL kit code. run_cases.py reads each case's identity block from the case file to build the simulated customer, so a case without 'identity' cannot be run.
items.quote: ident = {c["id"]: {"identity": c["identity"]} for c in cases}
items.notes: The page-captured copy (docs/reference/hackathon_practice_cases.json) has no identity block, so only kit/public-test-set.json (or a fixture copying its identity) is runnable.
